description: We are developing a lunar landing site planning tool using NASA data, lunar terrain analysis, and orbital calculations. Our focus is landing safety, sunlight, and Earth communication visibility. We welcome collaborators with skills in space engineering, AI, and visualization.
summary:
MoonFix is an interactive lunar landing-site planning tool that helps users explore how sunlight, Earth visibility, and terrain constraints affect potential mission windows near the Moon's south pole.

The application evaluates 10 candidate sites using 720 time-stamped reference samples across a 72-hour analysis period. Users can adjust safety thresholds, filter time intervals, rank candidate locations, examine continuous visibility windows, and compare two sites side by side.

MoonFix transforms complex lunar environmental data into an accessible decision-support interface. Rather than presenting a single ideal landing site, it allows users to explore trade-offs between illumination, communications, and terrain conditions.

Built as a browser-based application using HTML, CSS, and JavaScript, MoonFix supports interactive analysis, CSV exports, and reproducible comparisons. It is an educational and preliminary planning prototype, not a flight-qualified landing safety system.
details:
## The Challenge

Planning a mission near the Moon's south pole requires balancing sunlight availability, direct-to-Earth communication visibility, and local terrain conditions. Mountain ridges and crater walls can obstruct the Sun or Earth, complicating the identification of useful mission windows.

## Our Solution

MoonFix is an interactive, browser-based lunar mission planning prototype. It helps users compare 10 candidate landing locations through a visual interface that evaluates illumination, Earth visibility, terrain clearance, and local slope.

The application includes:

- An interactive schematic map of 10 lunar south-pole candidate sites.
- Adjustable mission start and end times.
- Terrain-clearance safety margins from 0° to 3°.
- Minimum continuous visibility-window and terrain-slope filters.
- Dynamic landing-site ranking.
- Solar and Earth visibility timelines.
- Side-by-side comparisons of two candidate sites.
- CSV exports and shareable scenario settings.

## How It Works

MoonFix analyzes 720 prepared scientific reference samples covering 72 hourly epochs from November 14–16, 2026, in the TDB time scale.

The reference data is associated with NASA/JPL Horizons Sun–Earth geometry and Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter LOLA-derived terrain information.

At each sample, the analysis engine calculates:

Sun Clearance = Sun Elevation − Local Sun Skyline − Safety Margin

Earth Clearance = Earth Elevation − Local Earth Skyline − Safety Margin

A sample meets the visibility condition when both clearances are nonnegative.

The system applies linear interpolation between hourly samples to estimate continuous intervals in which both conditions hold. Users can explore how different terrain margins, time intervals, and slope limits affect the results.

## Innovation and Impact

MoonFix combines multiple lunar environmental constraints into one accessible decision-support interface.

Rather than treating solar illumination and Earth communication visibility as separate problems, it shows how their intersection changes across locations and time.

Its interactive workflow makes complex lunar-planning concepts easier to explore for students, educators, researchers, and early-stage mission designers.

## Technology

MoonFix was developed using HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, SVG visualizations, and Python-based build tools. Node.js and Playwright were used for automated testing.

The application is self-contained and can operate offline without an external API, cloud backend, account, or installation.

## Scientific Limitations

The 720 reference samples were supplied from earlier research materials. Their original JPL Horizons requests, LOLA elevation-model preprocessing, and complete error budgets have not been independently reproduced in this release.

The model covers only the supplied dates. Its interpolated visibility windows are approximations, and the 72 hourly epochs define 71 intervening one-hour intervals.

MoonFix is an educational and preliminary mission-analysis tool, not a NASA-certified operational landing safety system. It does not validate communication link budgets, power storage requirements, or detailed landing hazards.
